sources.citation: ASJP (lexibank-asjp) list BALDEMU, compiled by Tessa de Mol-van Valen 2015 from Seignobos & Tourneux 1984 and Tourneux 1987.
sources.note: Nothing; 40-item ASJP transcription without stress or tone marks.

sources.citation: Gravina, Richard. 2014. The phonology of Proto-Central Chadic: the reconstruction of the phonology and lexicon of Proto-Central Chadic, and the linguistic history of the Central Chadic languages. Utrecht: LOT (LOT 375). Baldemu treated as 'Mbazla [bdn]', sec. 3.3.10 (p. 55-56) and sec. 5.3.4 (pp. 113-115).
sources.note: Nothing about Mbazla/Baldemu stress; the reconstruction explicitly excludes tone and stress. States (p. 113): 'No published phonology exists for any of these languages [Maroua group]... For Mbazla, the data amounts to a total of 390 entries from various sources of differing quality.' Notes word-final *n→ŋ in Mbazla and back-rounding vowel harmony largely attributable to labialized velars.

sources.citation: Brye, Edward. 2003. A rapid appraisal language survey of the Baldemu language (Diamare Division, Far North Province). SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2003-015. Dallas: SIL International. 13 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic rapid appraisal (fieldwork 15 Feb 2000; three elderly speakers located). Appendix B (pp. 7-12) is a 126-item ALCAM word list elicited by Domché-Teko with tone diacritics (acute/grave/macron, e.g. àráy 'eye', ŋgùzó' 'hair', kítīŋ 'nose') on every form; no phonology section, no mention of stress or accent. fetched sources from the Wayback snapshot of the SIL file (live SIL host returns Cloudflare 403).

sources.note: Nothing. Glottolog lists 8 references, none of hhtype grammar/phonology/sketch (n_desc_refs = 0). Wikipedia cites ALCAM 2012 (Binam Bikoi ed.), Brye 2003, Seignobos & Tourneux 1984, Tourneux 1987, MacEachern 2002, Gravina 2011; alternate names Mbazlam, Baldare, Baldamu, Balda, Mbazla.
